vulnerability.impact: ExifTool metadata processing remote code execution

entry_points: workhorse upload exif sanitizer decision (exif.go IsExifFile / rewrite.go) - file type is inferred from suffix only and ExifTool runs on non-JPEG/TIFF content (e.g. DjVu) before upload
lib/gitlab/sanitizers/exif.rb clean path - MIME/type check before invoking exiftool on uploaded images
ground_truth.fix_commit: Fixed via GitLab security release 13.10.3 (also 13.9.6 / 13.8.8). No single public upstream commit: GitLab fixed this in its private security branches; the mirrored v13.10.2...v13.10.3 tag diff (github.com/gitlabhq/gitlabhq) contains the two relevant fix commits efe45a03bff39d238a0fda1c273beca0295c48c9 (workhorse: check image content type before running exiftool; FileTypeFromSuffix + MIME checks) and 09b628c32e2c0bf54347745cf7d165cf987731c0 (lib/gitlab/sanitizers/exif.rb: clean only legitimate JPG/TIFF files via ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES). Pinned snapshot v13.10.2 is vulnerable.
ground_truth.finding_match_rule: TP: report identifies that uploaded image content is not validated to be legitimate JPG/TIFF before ExifTool runs (workhorse exif.go/rewrite.go or lib/gitlab/sanitizers/exif.rb), allowing an ExifTool DjVu annotation payload (CVE-2021-22204 underneath) to execute commands, names CVE-2021-22205, and attributes remote code execution on GitLab. Findings limited to the generic ExifTool CVE-2021-22204 without GitLab upload reachability are not TP.
ground_truth.safe_reproduction_predicate: Static predicate: v13.10.2 exif.rb/exif.go do not check MIME/type (IsExifFile only by extension), so a crafted DjVu/ExifTool payload file uploaded to an issue/avatar endpoint reaches ExifTool. Dynamic reproduction only in a disposable GitLab instance with outbound network blocked and with a benign ExifTool test image that prints a harmless marker; do not execute command payloads or touch production data.
